title: DISTINCTCOUNT of a one-side column counts the blank row's BLANK

source.quote: DISTINCTCOUNT function counts the BLANK value
DISTINCTCOUNT considers BLANK as a valid value, whereas
source.supports: BLANK is a valid value for DISTINCTCOUNT
but the same page gives DISTINCTCOUNT as COUNTROWS ( DISTINCT ( column ) ), and DISTINCT has no blank row

derivation: Product[Color] holds Red, Blue, Red: 2 distinct stored values. The blank row adds a BLANK value to the column, and DISTINCTCOUNT counts BLANK: 3.
alternative: If DISTINCTCOUNT is exactly COUNTROWS ( DISTINCT ( Product[Color] ) ), as dax.guide writes it, the blank row is not counted and the result is 2.
notes: The sources settle that a stored BLANK is counted (see distinctcount-counts-stored-blank). They do not say outright whether the blank row of an invalid relationship is.
